title: Sur les équations différentielles linéaires à coefficients périodiques
venue: Annales scientifiques de l’École Normale Supérieure
relevance: Original continuous-time periodic linear-system foundation.
novelty_threat: Floquet analysis itself is classical; applying a period map needs a distinct scientific question.
evidence_locator: Numdam bibliographic record.
limitations: Historical source; the project uses discrete updates, and no claim is made to have audited this French proof.

title: Learning long-term dependencies with gradient descent is difficult
relevance: Classical explanation of why learning distant dependencies is difficult.
novelty_threat: Long-horizon failure and gradient decay are established phenomena, not sufficient novelty.
evidence_locator: Original-paper first-page search extract and indexed abstract; publisher access blocked.
limitations: Optimization difficulty is not a theorem that a competent fixed-weight network must forget under repeated inference.
version_note: Institutional teaching copy of the author manuscript (title page says to appear); publication metadata refers to the final 1994 article.

title: How the brain keeps the eyes still
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 93(23): 13339-13344
relevance: Treats analog persistent memory as an attracting line of equilibria, explains tuned feedback and slow drift, and contrasts discrete noise-resistant point attractors.
novelty_threat: Continuous-memory neutral directions and the categorical/continuous distinction are classical foundations, not candidate novelty.
evidence_locator: Author-paper scan, pp. 13342-13343: Eq. (4)-(5), linear tuning/eigenvalue discussion, nonlinear approximation, and explicit line-versus-point-attractor contrast.
limitations: Exact manifold neutrality does not guarantee robustness to noise or mistuning. Expanded author name retains published H. initial; no unverified expansion.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
relevance: Introduces gated access to a persistent internal memory path and long-delay artificial tasks.
novelty_threat: Gating, persistent state, and delayed cue retention are foundational prior art.
evidence_locator: Author-hosted PDF, pp. 1–2, introduction and architectural motivation; relevant introductory sections inspected.
limitations: Original architecture and learning algorithm differ from modern forget-gate LSTMs; retention depends on the learned complete state.

title: The echo state approach to analysing and training recurrent neural networks - with an Erratum note
venue: GMD Report 148; corrected author version dated 2010
relevance: Introduces echo states as functions of left-infinite input history and readout training; includes periodic generators and multiple-switch examples.
novelty_threat: Initial-state forgetting while retaining input-history information is foundational, so these must not be conflated.
evidence_locator: Corrected PDF title page/erratum notice; Introduction and Definition 1, pp. 3-5.
limitations: 2010 author version corrects a flaw in Definition 3 and Proposition 1 of the 2001 report. Original theorem equivalences were not independently audited.

title: Short term memory in echo state networks
relevance: Foundational short-term-memory capacity reference for reconstruction of past inputs from recurrent states.
novelty_threat: A memory-capacity versus state-dimension statement needs this antecedent and its task/readout assumptions.
evidence_locator: Author-uploaded report title page: May 28, 2002; footnote: GMD Report 152, publication March 28, 2002. Author publication index labels the item 2001.
limitations: Year conflict in author index retained explicitly; 2002 follows report title-page publication note. Capacity theorem not read in this audit; Fraunhofer PDF endpoint timed out.

title: Short-Term Memory in Orthogonal Neural Networks
relevance: Studies retrieval of temporal sequences from the instantaneous state in linear discrete networks; orthogonal and distributed shift-register capacity scales with size.
novelty_threat: Preservation controls and claims connecting effective dimension to memory must compare established orthogonal-memory results.
evidence_locator: arXiv abstract, journal-reference and DOI fields.
limitations: Specific linear/noise/capacity normalization assumptions not audited from full text.

title: The Effective Rank: a Measure of Effective Dimensionality
relevance: Entropy-based effective rank provides a historical measurement reference.
novelty_threat: Normalized spectral dimension is an established diagnostic, not an information-retention theorem.
evidence_locator: Zenodo proceedings record.
limitations: Repository DOI; distinguish normalized singular-value entropy from covariance-eigenvalue entropy.

title: Memory traces in dynamical systems
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 105(48):18970–18975
relevance: Measures retained input information relative to noise with a Fisher memory curve.
novelty_threat: Noise-aware dynamical memory measures and normal/nonnormal distinctions long predate participation-ratio comparisons.
evidence_locator: Author PDF pp. 18970-18971: Fisher Memory Matrix, Eq. (1)-(5); normal-network memory curve and sum rule.
limitations: Local input sensitivity and explicitly specified dynamical noise; bounds depend on input/noise/weight normalization. Does not equate covariance rank with nonlinear global memory.

title: The Graph Neural Network Model
relevance: Early graph-state recurrence and contraction-based computation.
novelty_threat: Treating GNN computation as recurrent state dynamics is foundational prior art.
evidence_locator: Publisher-indexed abstract and Crossref metadata.
limitations: Historical graph-state architecture, not a periodic temporal-graph cue-retention experiment.

title: Short-term memory in neuronal networks through dynamical compressed sensing
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 23
relevance: Sparse signal structure allows memory reconstruction beyond a naive neuron-count bound.
novelty_threat: Dimension reduction can preserve reconstructible structured memory; storage dimension is not an unconditional capacity proxy.
evidence_locator: Official NeurIPS abstract, including sparsity and orthogonal-network qualifications.
limitations: Sparse-sequence reconstruction uses assumptions different from smoothly storing independent continuous tags.

title: Stimulus-dependent suppression of chaos in recurrent neural networks
relevance: Mean-field theory links oscillatory drive amplitude and frequency to suppression of chaotic fluctuations and phase locking.
novelty_threat: Input-induced stabilization and frequency-selective chaos suppression precede a generic Floquet-collapse claim.
evidence_locator: Abstract; bibliographic header; Eq. (1)-(3) and Fig. 1 inspected to verify model/driver definition.
limitations: Random continuous-time rate circuits; no required-history recall endpoint. Deep mean-field derivation not reviewed. Abbott's expanded first name verified from Columbia.

title: Finding structure with randomness: Probabilistic algorithms for constructing approximate matrix decompositions
relevance: Randomized methods approximate dominant matrix decompositions.
novelty_threat: Matrix-free spectral estimation is an implementation tool, not scientific novelty here.

title: Fundamental limits on persistent activity in networks of noisy neurons
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 109(43): 17645-17650
relevance: Bounds noise-induced diffusion of continuously stored memory using an information-diffusion relation.
novelty_threat: Neutral tangent directions alone cannot support claims of robust memory; continuous-attractor noise limits are prior theory.
evidence_locator: Abstract; Results model assumptions and Diffusive Drift due to Ongoing Neural Noise inspected.
limitations: Poisson spiking/weak-fluctuation approximation and tuned-away systematic drift; supporting derivations not deeply audited.

title: Information Processing Capacity of Dynamical Systems
relevance: Defines target-function capacities and a qualified total-capacity relation to independent state variables.
novelty_threat: Task-aligned capacity, state dimension, and computation/memory tradeoffs have an established quantitative framework.
evidence_locator: PMC full text, definitions of capacity, orthogonal target functions, and maximum-capacity discussion.
limitations: Bounds rely on target/input assumptions and linear readouts; covariance participation ratio is not their capacity.

title: Echo State Property Linked to an Input: Exploring a Fundamental Characteristic of Recurrent Neural Networks
relevance: Input-specific ESP distinguishes dependence on input history from arbitrary initial conditions. Uniform shrinking bounds imply uniqueness; a periodic driver with ESP has a response whose period divides the input period.
novelty_threat: The proposed unique forced response and history-washout foundations are standard input-dependent synchronization theory.
evidence_locator: Definition 2.2, author-PDF p. 5; Lemma 2.2, pp. 7-8; Proposition 2.3 and proof, p. 9; Section 2.1 cautions on folklore.
limitations: Compact state space and entire-solution definitions. Contraction bound is sufficient; negative local exponents alone do not establish global uniqueness. First name expanded using university author record.

title: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks
venue: ICML; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 28(3):1310–1318

novelty_threat: A collapse experiment must distinguish failed learning from inference-time loss in a trained competent model.
evidence_locator: Official PMLR abstract and publication metadata.
limitations: Gradient clipping and optimization findings do not establish periodic-driver-specific memory loss.
